entries.title: Successful call authorized with SOROBAN_CREDENTIALS_ADDRESS_V2
entries.why: Protocol 27 adds the ADDRESS_V2 credentials arm. Readers generated before it cannot decode the authorization entry, and readers that switch only on ADDRESS treat the entry as unknown.

entries.title: Address credentials with delegates whose own nested delegate also signs (CAP-0071)
entries.why: SOROBAN_CREDENTIALS_ADDRESS_WITH_DELEGATES carries delegate signatures, and each delegate may carry nested delegates. Here the authorizing custom account forwards to its delegate, which forwards to its own delegate: three __check_auth calls, one nonce (the authorizing account's). Readers built on older XDR fail to decode the credentials; readers that treat delegates as authorizers with nonces misreport them.

entries.title: Native Stellar Asset Contract transfer to a non-existent account creates the account
entries.why: A native SAC transfer to a G address that does not exist creates the account entry with the transferred balance; there is no CreateAccount operation. Readers that only record account creation from CreateAccount miss the new account.

entries.title: XLM SAC transfer to a non-existent account creating it with no CreateAccount operation, on both passphrases
entries.why: From Protocol 26 an XLM transfer through the Stellar Asset Contract to an account that does not exist creates it. The ledger has an account creation with no CreateAccount operation; readers that only record account creation from that operation miss the new account.

entries.title: SAC transfer from an account whose trustline was deleted earlier in the same ledger fails
entries.why: A payment empties a trustline, a ChangeTrust deletes it, and a SAC transfer of that asset in the same ledger then fails. Readers that resolve the transfer against state from the start of the ledger record a movement that did not happen.

entries.title: SAC transfer from an account merged earlier in the same ledger fails
entries.why: An AccountMerge removes the account, and a later transaction in the same ledger that uses it as the SAC transfer's source fails before applying (op_no_account). Readers that assume a valid-looking envelope applied record a transfer from a removed account.

entries.title: SAC transfer to an account merged earlier in the same ledger fails
entries.why: An AccountMerge removes the destination, and a SAC transfer to it later in the same ledger traps. Readers that credit the destination from the envelope record a credit to an account that no longer exists.

entries.title: Stellar Asset Contract trust creates a trustline with no ChangeTrust operation and no event
entries.why: The trustline appears only as a created ledger entry under an InvokeHostFunction operation. There is no ChangeTrust operation and the contract emits no event, so readers that derive trustlines from classic operations or from events never see it.

entries.title: Stellar Asset Contract trust for a contract address succeeds and creates nothing
entries.why: A contract holds its Stellar Asset Contract balance in the contract's own storage, never in a trustline, so trust(C…) returns at once: success, no authorization, no ledger-entry change. A reader that derives a trustline from the call's argument invents one for an address that cannot have trustlines.

entries.title: Stellar Asset Contract trust for an account that already has the trustline changes nothing
entries.why: trust is idempotent: when the trustline exists it returns without requiring authorization and writes no ledger entry. A reader that turns every trust call into a created trustline, or into an authorization change, reports a change that did not happen.

entries.title: Stepwise Protocol 23 to 24 upgrade on the public passphrase adding 31,879,035 stroops to the fee pool
entries.why: On the public passphrase the Protocol 24 upgrade adds 31,879,035 stroops to the header's fee pool with no ledger-entry change and no transaction. Readers that reconcile the fee pool from fee charges alone, or that assume upgrades only change entries, find the numbers do not add up.

entries.title: ConfigUpgradeSet holding CONFIG_SETTING_FREEZE_BYPASS_TXS_DELTA, the upgrade-set bytes stellar-core stores in contract data
entries.why: From protocol 26 the list of transactions allowed to bypass frozen keys (CAP-0077) changes through a delta: hashes to add and hashes to remove. stellar-core applies the delta to the stored CONFIG_SETTING_FREEZE_BYPASS_TXS entry and never stores the delta, so the only place a ledger holds this arm is the ConfigUpgradeSet kept as SCV_BYTES contract data before the upgrade. Readers that decode those bytes and know only the stored setting arms reject them.

entries.title: ConfigUpgradeSet holding CONFIG_SETTING_FROZEN_LEDGER_KEYS_DELTA, the upgrade-set bytes stellar-core stores in contract data
entries.why: From protocol 26 the frozen ledger keys setting (CAP-0077) changes through a delta: keys to freeze and keys to unfreeze. stellar-core applies the delta to the stored CONFIG_SETTING_FROZEN_LEDGER_KEYS entry and never stores the delta, so the only place a ledger holds this arm is the ConfigUpgradeSet kept as SCV_BYTES contract data before the upgrade. Readers that decode those bytes and know only the stored setting arms reject them.

entries.title: Configuration upgrade setting the frozen-ledger-keys list (keys stored as encoded bytes)
entries.why: The frozen-keys configuration setting holds ledger keys as EncodedLedgerKey byte strings inside a CONFIG_SETTING entry, changed by a configuration upgrade with no transaction. Readers that decode config settings with a closed list of arms, or expect keys as structured XDR, fail on it.

entries.title: ClaimClaimableBalance failing with CLAIM_CLAIMABLE_BALANCE_TRUSTLINE_FROZEN
entries.why: Protocol 26 adds frozen ledger keys and new result codes for operations that touch them. A claim whose trustline is frozen fails with claim_claimable_balance.trustline_frozen. Readers with a closed table of result codes fail to map it.

entries.title: LiquidityPoolDeposit whose LX trustline key is frozen fails while applying with TRUSTLINE_FROZEN
entries.why: CAP-0077 freezes ledger keys through a configuration upgrade. For a pool deposit stellar-core checks the asset trustlines against the frozen keys only while applying, so the transaction enters the ledger and fails with LIQUIDITY_POOL_DEPOSIT_TRUSTLINE_FROZEN, a result arm older readers do not know.

entries.title: LiquidityPoolWithdraw whose LX trustline key is frozen fails while applying with TRUSTLINE_FROZEN
entries.why: As for deposits, a withdrawal's asset trustlines are checked against CAP-0077's frozen keys only while applying, so it reaches the ledger and fails with LIQUIDITY_POOL_WITHDRAW_TRUSTLINE_FROZEN; HZ keeps its pool shares.

entries.title: LedgerHeader whose scpValue is STELLAR_VALUE_EMPTY_TX_SET: txSetHash zero, the proposed set in proposedValue
entries.why: From protocol 28 a validator that cannot download a nominated transaction set in time may vote for an empty one (CAP-0083): the header's txSetHash is all zeros and the set that was proposed moves into ext.proposedValue with the previous ledger's hash and version. Readers that take scpValue.txSetHash as the applied set's hash, or that know only the BASIC and SIGNED ext arms, misread or reject such a ledger.

entries.title: Muxed-contract strkey from contract ID and ID 2^63 equals the SEP-0023 test vector
entries.why: In XDR the 64-bit ID comes before the key in MuxedEd25519Account and MuxedContract, while the SEP-0023 strkey payload puts the key first; code that copies bytes between the two forms instead of converting field by field produces a valid-looking address for another key and ID.

entries.title: SCAddress MuxedContract{id, contractId} renders as a W address with the contract first
entries.why: In XDR the 64-bit ID comes before the key in MuxedEd25519Account and MuxedContract, while the SEP-0023 strkey payload puts the key first; code that copies bytes between the two forms instead of converting field by field produces a valid-looking address for another key and ID.

entries.title: MuxedAccount med25519{id, ed25519} renders as an M address with the key first
entries.why: In XDR the 64-bit ID comes before the key in MuxedEd25519Account and MuxedContract, while the SEP-0023 strkey payload puts the key first; code that copies bytes between the two forms instead of converting field by field produces a valid-looking address for another key and ID.

entries.title: SAC transfer from the issuer to a muxed contract address is emitted as a mint carrying to_muxed_id
entries.why: When the issuer transfers its own asset, the SAC emits a mint event, not a transfer; with a W destination the mint's data carries to_muxed_id. Readers that look for to_muxed_id only on transfer events, or that require a from topic, lose the routing.

entries.title: SAC mint to a muxed contract address that fails
entries.why: A SAC mint whose destination is a W address fails and the transaction traps; no event and no balance change. Readers that credit the destination from the envelope's arguments record a mint that never happened.

entries.title: muxed_id host function on a muxed contract address (W…): the call returns u64 42
entries.why: Protocol 30 (CAP-84) added SC_ADDRESS_TYPE_MUXED_CONTRACT, written W…: a contract address with a 64-bit routing ID, and host functions that read the ID. Here a contract is called with the W… form of its own address and returns its ID, 42, so the envelope carries the new ScAddress arm. Readers built on older XDR cannot decode the transaction set at all; readers that decode it must keep the W… argument and the returned u64 intact.

entries.title: Native Stellar Asset Contract transfer to a muxed contract address (W...) at Protocol 30
entries.why: Protocol 30 adds ScAddress::MuxedContract, rendered as a 69-character W address. The envelope's destination argument is W, but the event's to topic is the plain C contract and the muxed ID is in to_muxed_id. Readers built before Protocol 30 cannot decode the argument, and readers that store addresses in fixed-width columns cannot hold it.

entries.title: SAC transfers to W addresses with muxed IDs 2^63 and 2^64 - 1, on both passphrases
entries.why: A Stellar Asset Contract transfer to a muxed contract address (W…) credits the plain contract: the event's to topic is the C address and the ID travels as to_muxed_id in a data map. IDs at 2^63 and 2^64 - 1 do not fit a signed 64-bit integer or a JavaScript number. Readers that store the W form as the account, drop the ID or overflow it misreport the transfer.

entries.title: 116-byte bucket record: INITENTRY of contract data keyed by SCV_EXECUTABLE_TAG, which Protocol 27 XDR cannot decode
entries.why: A history-archive bucket holds every live ledger entry, including other people's contract data, so a catch-up reader decodes entries it never asked for. This record is the contract data entry created in cap-0085/contract-data-keyed-by-executable-tag, merged into a level 6 bucket: its key uses SCV_EXECUTABLE_TAG (ScVal arm 22, added in Protocol 28), and a decoder built on Protocol 27 XDR rejects it with an invalid-value error and cannot restore the checkpoint at all.

entries.title: Contract data created under an SCV_EXECUTABLE_TAG key ("pocket"), the ScVal arm added in Protocol 28
entries.why: Protocol 28 (CAP-85) added SCV_EXECUTABLE_TAG (ScVal arm 22). Here a contract stores a persistent entry whose key is ExecutableTag("pocket") and whose value is a 32-byte hash. Decoders built on Protocol 27 XDR reject the whole ledger (and every bucket holding the entry) as invalid.

entries.title: SCV_EXECUTABLE_TAG passed as an argument and published as contract event data
entries.why: Event data is any SCVal, and from Protocol 30 that includes SCV_EXECUTABLE_TAG (CAP-85). Readers that map event data through a fixed list of SCVal arms, or that learned the new arm only from storage keys, reject or drop this event.

entries.title: SCV_EXECUTABLE_TAG passed as an argument and returned as the Soroban return value
entries.why: SorobanTransactionMeta.returnValue is any SCVal; from Protocol 30 it can be SCV_EXECUTABLE_TAG (CAP-85). Readers that convert return values through a fixed list of arms, or decoders built on pre-30 definitions, cannot read this transaction's meta.

entries.title: SCV_EXECUTABLE_TAG stored as the value of a persistent contract-data entry keyed by a symbol
entries.why: Real ledgers show SCV_EXECUTABLE_TAG (Protocol 30, CAP-85) only as a contract-data key and in footprints. Here a contract takes the tag as an argument and stores it as an entry's value, so the arm appears in the envelope's arguments and in a CREATED contract-data value; readers that accept the arm only where keys are decoded fail on it.

entries.title: Contract instance created with executable EXTERNAL_REF {owner, tag "pocket"} (Protocol 28)
entries.why: CAP-85 added CONTRACT_EXECUTABLE_EXTERNAL_REF: a contract instance whose code is found through another contract's ExecutableTag entry. A factory call creates such an instance here. Decoders built on Protocol 27 XDR cannot decode the instance, and readers that expect every instance to name a wasm hash or the Stellar Asset Contract mis-classify the deployment.

entries.title: External-ref contract instance updated by set_owner under Secp256k1 custom-account authorization
entries.why: An update of a CONTRACT_EXECUTABLE_EXTERNAL_REF instance: set_owner rewrites the instance storage, authorized by the instance itself as a custom account with a Secp256k1 signature map. Readers on Protocol 27 XDR cannot decode the instance on either side of the change, and readers that expect ed25519 signatures in address credentials mis-decode the authorization.

entries.title: SCV_BYTES call arguments of 2592 and 4627 bytes (ML-DSA-87 key and signature sizes)
entries.why: Post-quantum key and signature sizes reach ledgers only as plain bytes arguments; there is no signer-key or signature XDR for them. Readers with small fixed buffers or length limits for byte arguments fail.

entries.title: First ledger whose StellarValue uses the STELLAR_VALUE_SIGNED_MS arm with a millisecond close time
entries.why: Protocol 30 adds arm 3 (STELLAR_VALUE_SIGNED_MS) to StellarValue.ext, carrying closeTimeMs. Every ledger after the upgrade ledger uses it, so a decoder generated before Protocol 30 rejects the whole LedgerCloseMeta at the ledger header, and an indexer built on one stops at this ledger.

entries.title: Ledger closing in the same whole second as its predecessor, with a transaction expiring at that second
entries.why: With millisecond close times, two consecutive ledgers can share closeTime and differ only in closeTimeMs. A transaction whose maxTime equals the current second still applies. Readers that assume close times strictly increase, or compare time bounds against milliseconds, mis-order the ledgers or misjudge the bound.

entries.title: Empty ledger closing within the same whole second as the previous ledger
entries.why: Ledger 3 closes in the same whole second as ledger 2, so closeTime is equal and only closeTimeMs differs; the test's transaction with minSeqAge 1 is rejected because the age is still 0. Readers that assume closeTime strictly increases between ledgers mis-order or merge them.

entries.title: Ordinary Protocol 30 ledger from a local core: STELLAR_VALUE_SIGNED_MS and LedgerCloseMeta ext.v1
entries.why: From Protocol 30 the StellarValue carries the close time in milliseconds inside a new signed arm. These local twins give both real passphrases the shape the network ledgers have, so a reader can be tested on each without network history.

entries.title: LedgerHeader whose scpValue is STELLAR_VALUE_EMPTY_TX_SET_MS: zero txSetHash, closeTimeMs in proposedMsValue
entries.why: The protocol 30 form of the empty-set vote (CAP-0083 with CAP-0088 millisecond close times): ext arm 4 carries closeTimeMs next to the proposed set's hash, the previous ledger's hash and version. Readers that read closeTimeMs only from the SIGNED_MS arm fall back to whole seconds on these ledgers, and readers built before XDR 30 cannot decode arm 4 at all.

entries.title: Protocol 30 ledger whose millisecond close time is not a whole second (closeTimeMs 1794475923913)
entries.why: With the SIGNED_MS StellarValue arm the close time has millisecond precision: here closeTimeMs is 1794475923913 while closeTime is 1794475923, so the two differ by 913 ms. Readers that derive one from the other by multiplying, or that store whole seconds only, report a time that is off by up to a second.

entries.title: Protocol 30 upgrade ledger: header at 30 but StellarValue still in the whole-second SIGNED arm
entries.why: The ledger that carries the Protocol 30 upgrade already has ledgerVersion 30 in its header, but its StellarValue was agreed before the upgrade and still uses the SIGNED arm with only a whole-second closeTime. Readers that switch to millisecond close times by header version expect closeTimeMs here and find none.

entries.title: AccountMerge of an AUTH_IMMUTABLE account fails with ACCOUNT_MERGE_IMMUTABLE_SET
entries.why: An account with AUTH_IMMUTABLE can never be merged; the merge fails while applying and the account and its balance stay. A reader that treats a merge in the envelope as done removes an account that still exists.

entries.title: AccountMerge into an account whose native buying liabilities leave no room fails with ACCOUNT_MERGE_DEST_FULL
entries.why: A destination's room for native is INT64_MAX minus its balance minus its buying liabilities. DF's open offer buys 9,223,372,030,000,000,000 stroops of XLM, so a merge of 1,000 XLM no longer fits and fails while applying, although DF's balance is only about 100 XLM. Readers that check only the balance cannot explain the failure, and readers that apply the merge from the envelope move 1,000 XLM that never moved.

entries.title: Issued-asset payment of 2^53 + 1 stroops leaving both balances at 2^53 + 1
entries.why: 9007199254740993 is the smallest positive integer a float64 cannot hold, so a reader that parses amounts or balances as JSON numbers or doubles stores 9007199254740992 for the payment and both trustline balances.

entries.title: Text memo with the non-UTF-8 bytes ff fe survives a native round trip, or is refused
entries.why: An XDR string is a byte string and stellar-core does not validate MEMO_TEXT, so ledgers hold text memos that are not UTF-8; an SDK that turns them into a native string and back replaces the bytes, and the rebuilt memo no longer matches the signed transaction.

entries.title: Manage-sell-offer with offer ID 2^53+1 passed as a native number: exact or refused
entries.why: 2^53+1 is a valid offer ID but not a safe IEEE-754 double: a JavaScript number literal is already 9007199254740992 before the SDK sees it, so an SDK must encode the exact ID or refuse the number.

entries.title: Manage-sell-offer with offer ID 2^53+1 passed as a decimal string: encoded exactly
entries.why: The control of the unsafe-number vector: 2^53+1 is a valid offer ID, and passed as a decimal string it is never rounded, so every SDK that takes a string ID must encode exactly 9007199254740993. A refusal or another ID here means the defect is in the string path, not in JavaScript's number type.

entries.title: Manage-sell-offer with offer ID 2^64 (beyond int64) must be refused
entries.why: ManageSellOfferOp.offerID is an int64 that stellar-core requires to be non-negative; a builder that accepts a value outside that range encodes another offer ID, so the operation edits or deletes a different offer, or is refused as malformed.

entries.why: ManageSellOfferOp.offerID is an int64 that stellar-core requires to be non-negative; a builder that accepts a value outside that range encodes another offer ID, so the operation edits or deletes a different offer, or is refused as malformed.

entries.title: Transaction failed at apply time with txBAD_AUTH after an earlier transaction zeroed its master key
entries.why: Signatures are checked again when a transaction is applied, against the signers as an earlier transaction of the same ledger left them. A transaction that failed with txBAD_AUTH at apply time has consumed its sequence number and paid its fee but has no operation results; readers that treat txBAD_AUTH as a submission-only code, or expect a sequence number to stay, misreport it.

entries.title: Transaction failed at apply time with txBAD_AUTH_EXTRA after an earlier transaction made one of its signatures unnecessary
entries.why: XA's transaction carries XA's and Y's signatures for an operation whose source is Y. The transaction applied first adds XA as a signer of Y, so when XA's transaction is applied XA's signature alone meets Y's threshold and Y's goes unused. Signature checks are repeated while applying; readers that treat txBAD_AUTH_EXTRA as a submission-only error cannot place it in a ledger.

entries.title: Transaction failed at apply time with txBAD_MIN_SEQ_AGE_OR_GAP after an earlier no-op bump moved its source's seqLedger
entries.why: GA's transaction asks for min_seq_ledger_gap 1 (CAP-0021). The transaction applied first bumps GA's sequence number to 1, below its current one: the number does not change, but GA's seqLedger becomes this ledger, so GA's transaction now comes too early. Readers that evaluate preconditions from the envelope and the previous ledger's state call this transaction valid.

entries.title: Transaction failed at apply time with txBAD_SEQ after an earlier transaction bumped its source's sequence
entries.why: A transaction that was valid when the set was built can still fail with txBAD_SEQ when an earlier transaction of the same ledger moved its source's sequence number. It pays its fee, consumes no sequence number and has no operation results; readers that assume failed transactions never reach a ledger, or that read the sequence number from the envelope, get it wrong.

entries.title: Transaction failed at apply time with txNO_ACCOUNT after an earlier transaction merged its source away
entries.why: MA's transaction was valid when the set was built; MB's transaction, applied first, merges MA into MB. MA's fee was already taken, so the merged balance is 999,999,900 stroops, and MA's own transaction then finds no source account. Readers that assume a failed transaction's source still exists, or look up its account to attribute the fee, fail here.

entries.title: Operation failed at apply time with opBAD_AUTH after an earlier transaction zeroed its source's master key
entries.why: OY's transaction has an operation whose source is OX, signed by OX's master key. The transaction applied first sets OX's master weight to 0, so that operation's signature no longer counts and the transaction fails with txFAILED and opBAD_AUTH, an OperationResult arm with no operation-specific result. Readers that expect every failed operation to carry its operation type's result trip on it.

entries.title: Payments of AlphaNum12 `ABCDE` (seven trailing NULs) and AlphaNum4 `ABCD` from one issuer
entries.why: A five-character code must be an AlphaNum12 padded with seven NULs, and it sits next to a different asset whose four-character code is its prefix. Readers that trim, truncate to four bytes or key assets by code text without the type merge the two.

entries.title: Payment of an issued AlphaNum4 asset whose code is `xlm`
entries.why: stellar-core accepts `xlm` as an issued asset code (letters and digits only), and it is unrelated to the native asset. Readers and SDKs that treat any asset named XLM as native, or rename it, credit lumens or re-encode different bytes.

entries.title: ChangeTrust whose line is the native asset, accepted before Protocol 10 and failed with txINTERNAL_ERROR
entries.why: Before Protocol 10 stellar-core let a ChangeTrust with the native asset as its line through validation and threw while applying it, so the ledger holds the native arm of the trust-line asset union with a txINTERNAL_ERROR result and no operation results. Readers that assume a trust line always names a credit asset or a pool, or that expect operation results on every failed transaction, break on it.

entries.title: change_trust that sets an existing trustline's limit to its current value (INT64_MAX): the trustline is written back unchanged
entries.why: Transaction 24846775… is a change_trust on an existing COPPER trustline with the limit it already has (9223372036854775807). stellar-core writes the trustline back with the same limit, balance and flags (only last_modified_ledger_seq moves), so no trustline limit change happened. A reader that builds a limit change from the operation body instead of comparing the entry before and after records an update that did not happen.

entries.title: CreateAccount operations funded by the network root account, whose key differs per passphrase
entries.why: The root account's key is derived from the network ID, so the same funding transaction has a different source on each passphrase while every created account is the same. Readers or fixtures that hard-code one network's root, or derive it from the wrong passphrase, attribute the funding to the wrong account.

entries.title: A failed and a successful path payment with identical envelope amounts in one ledger
entries.why: Two path payments with the same send_max and dest_amount meet one offer: the first consumes it and moves value, the second fails with TOO_FEW_OFFERS and moves nothing. Readers that take amounts from the envelope instead of the results and ledger changes report a payment that never happened.

entries.title: Failed transaction whose second operation's own code is success: payment SUCCESS inside txFAILED is rolled back
entries.why: Transaction 34a69fbc… failed with txFAILED: its first operation (path_payment_strict_send) failed with UNDER_DESTMIN, and its second (a payment of 1 DENEB to the asset's issuer) carries the result code PAYMENT_SUCCESS. stellar-core rolled both back: the transaction has no operation meta, and only the fee and the sequence number bump took effect. A reader that takes an operation's success from its own result code alone records the payment as successful (or as a movement) although nothing happened.

entries.title: Transaction authorised only by two hash-x preimages of 0 and 64 bytes
entries.why: For a hash-x signer the DecoratedSignature carries the preimage itself, here empty and 64 bytes long, with a hint taken from its sha256. Readers that expect every signature to be a 64-byte ed25519 signature reject the empty one or misattribute both.

entries.title: ManageData with a 64-byte value holding 00, ff and invalid UTF-8
entries.why: A data entry's value is up to 64 opaque bytes, not text. Readers that store it as a string drop the NUL, replace the invalid UTF-8 or cut the value short, and then cannot return what is on the ledger.

entries.title: ManageData with dataValue null removes the data entry
entries.why: A ManageData operation whose value is absent deletes the entry instead of setting an empty value. Readers that treat the operation as always writing a value record an empty string where the ledger shows a removed entry.

entries.title: manage_data that writes an existing data entry's current 64-byte value: the entry is written back unchanged
entries.why: Transaction c62a0535… is a manage_data that sets the data entry "wde" of GAMTT3RZ… to the 64-byte value it already holds. stellar-core writes the entry back as an update with the same value (only last_modified_ledger_seq moves). A reader that treats every write as a value change records a change of value that did not happen.

entries.title: ManageSellOffer deleting offer ID INT64_MAX fails with NOT_FOUND
entries.why: An offer ID of INT64_MAX passes every stateless check and fails only at apply. Readers that hold offer IDs as float64 round it to another ID, and readers that act on the operation rather than the result delete an offer that never existed.

entries.title: Transaction envelope carrying muxed id 2^64-1 and offer id 2^63-1, the largest values both fields hold
entries.why: The muxed id is unsigned 64-bit and the offer id signed 64-bit; a reader that holds either in a float64 or the wrong signedness decodes a different id. Every SDK tested round-trips these bytes, so the entry is the positive control for the 64-bit ID encoders.

entries.title: Transaction with 100 operations, 20 used signatures and a 28-byte text memo
entries.why: Each of the three vectors is at its maximum at once: 100 operations, 20 signatures from 20 accounts and a 28-byte memo. Readers with fixed buffers, a lower operation cap or a row per signature limit drop operations, signatures or memo bytes, and a 100-movement transaction exposes per-transaction batching limits.

entries.title: SetOptions setting AUTH_REQUIRED on an AUTH_IMMUTABLE account fails with SET_OPTIONS_CANT_CHANGE
entries.why: Once AUTH_IMMUTABLE is set an account's authorization flags can never change; the operation fails while applying. A reader that applies the envelope's set_flags to its account model reports flags the account does not have.

entries.title: SetOptions setting a home domain of the maximum 32 bytes
entries.why: The home domain is a string of at most 32 bytes. A reader that sizes its column below that, or validates it as a domain name, truncates or drops a value stellar-core accepted.

entries.title: SetOptions setting the master weight and the low, medium and high thresholds
entries.why: The thresholds are four bytes packed in one opaque field, ordered master weight, low, medium, high. Readers that decode them in another order, or as a signed integer, report the wrong signing requirements.

entries.title: SetOptions adding a twenty-first signer fails with SET_OPTIONS_TOO_MANY_SIGNERS
entries.why: An account holds at most 20 signers, and stellar-core finds out only when applying the operation. The failed operation's envelope still names the new signer; a reader that records signer additions from envelopes adds a signer that does not exist.

entries.title: set_options that sets the low threshold to its current value while it lowers medium and high: low stays 1
entries.why: Inner transaction 0740c64a… of fee bump 7535dbce… removes a trustline, then a set_options moves the thresholds from 00010202 to 00010101: medium and high go from 2 to 1, the low threshold is set to 1 and was already 1. Two more set_options remove two signers. Only medium and high changed; a reader that writes one row per threshold named in the operation body records a low-threshold change that did not happen.

entries.title: A trustline removed and created again by two transactions in one ledger
entries.why: Two transactions in one ledger change the same trustline: the first removes it (limit 0), the second creates it again. A reader that aggregates a ledger's changes per trustline, or keys a balance row by account and asset without ordering, keeps a stale row or loses the re-created trustline.

entries.title: Ledger with a transaction whose result is txINTERNAL_ERROR next to a successful one (stellar-core golden)
entries.why: stellar-core sets txINTERNAL_ERROR when applying a transaction throws; the transaction keeps its place in the ledger, pays its fee and has no operation results. A release core does this only on an unexpected fault, so the arm is rare enough that readers never meet it in testing; this golden ledger is from stellar-core's own test, which forces the fault with the memo text txINTERNAL_ERROR.

entries.title: Contract spec as a bare SCSpecEntry stream without a Wasm module
entries.why: Tools that keep or pass a spec without its Wasm hold the bare stream: entries appended with no frame or count, so the reader must decode entries until the bytes end.

entries.title: Contract spec with element counts past the bounds XDR v30 removed
entries.why: XDR v30 removed the bounds on function inputs (10), struct fields (40) and union and enum cases (50); a reader on older definitions refuses an interface any v30 tool writes.

entries.title: Contract spec whose function names user-defined types the spec never defines
entries.why: Spec shaking can drop type definitions a function still names; a reader that resolves every UDT at parse time refuses the whole interface, while the XDR itself is valid.

entries.title: Contract spec with event entries in every data format
entries.why: Event entries (SEP-48 v1.1) carry prefix topics, params located in the topic list or the data, and a data format; readers written before events existed skip or refuse them.

entries.title: Contract spec with every SCSpecEntry kind and every SCSpecTypeDef arm
entries.why: A spec reader that maps each entry kind and type to its own model drops or mislabels the arms it does not know; one function taking every type, a struct, a union with void and tuple cases, an enum, an error enum and an event exercise all of them at once.

entries.title: Testnet code built by soroban-sdk 30 with fully qualified 63-byte UDT names
entries.why: soroban-sdk 30 writes UDT names such as ::soroban_sdk::auth::CreateContractWithConstructorHostFnContext (63 bytes); readers on XDR older than v30 (name bound 60) refuse the whole interface.

entries.title: Contract spec whose struct and union refer to themselves
entries.why: Readers and binding generators that resolve user-defined types eagerly recurse without end on a struct holding an option of itself or a union holding a vector of itself.

entries.title: Mainnet contract code with no contractspecv0 section at all
entries.why: Contract code need not carry a spec; a reader that reports a missing section as a parse failure conflates code without an interface with a broken interface and may stop on it.

entries.title: Testnet fungible token whose SEP-41 functions use other parameter names
entries.why: Soroban arguments are positional, so a token may name balance's parameter account and approve's live_until_ledger; readers that match SEP-41 by parameter names misclassify it.

entries.title: Wasm spec section with three bytes after its last whole entry
entries.why: A stream reader that stops at the first incomplete entry without an error accepts bytes that are not a spec; the section must decode to whole entries with nothing left over.

entries.title: Wasm whose contractspecv0 section is cut short inside its last entry
entries.why: A reader that keeps the entries it decoded before the cut shows an interface the contract never declared in full; the stream does not decode to whole entries, so a correct reader refuses it.

entries.title: Wasm with two contractspecv0 custom sections, one function in each
entries.why: SEP-48 stores the interface in one contractspecv0 section, but the network never checks custom sections; readers that take the first section, the last, or both show different interfaces for the same code, so a second section can hide functions from one tool and show them in another.

entries.title: Contract spec with a 1024-byte struct name, exactly SC_SPEC_TYPE_NAME_LIMIT
entries.why: A name at the v30 bound must decode; readers with their own, smaller name limits refuse it.

entries.title: Contract spec with a 1025-byte struct name, one past SC_SPEC_TYPE_NAME_LIMIT
entries.why: A reader that does not enforce the declared maximum of a name accepts a spec the definitions forbid.

entries.title: Contract spec with a 60-byte struct name, the bound before XDR v30
entries.why: 60 bytes was SC_SPEC_TYPE_NAME_LIMIT until XDR v30; every reader must accept a name at the old bound.

entries.title: Contract spec with a 61-byte struct name, one past the pre-v30 bound
entries.why: XDR v30 raised SC_SPEC_TYPE_NAME_LIMIT from 60 to 1024 (soroban-sdk 30 writes fully qualified names); a reader on older definitions refuses the whole interface over one name.

entries.title: LEDGER_UPGRADE_BASE_FEE from 100 to 200 in a ledger whose payment is still charged 100
entries.why: pubnet and testnet have never changed their base fee, so no public ledger holds LedgerUpgrade arm 2. Upgrades apply after the ledger's transactions: the header of this ledger already says 200 while its payment was charged 100, so a reader that computes fees from the header of the same ledger gets them wrong.

entries.title: LEDGER_UPGRADE_CONFIG ledger: STATE/UPDATED pairs for every setting of the applied set
entries.why: A configuration upgrade changes Soroban settings with no transaction: the ledger's upgrade meta holds a STATE and an UPDATED change per setting, in no fixed order, and the cost-parameter arrays grow with the protocol (95 entries at Protocol 30, 86 at 28). Readers that look for setting changes only in transaction meta, or that index the change list by position, miss or misplace them.

entries.title: LedgerCloseMeta v2 of a ledger with no transactions and no upgrades
entries.why: A ledger can close with no transaction at all: both transaction-set phases are empty, there is no TransactionMeta, and nothing changes. Readers that expect at least one transaction, or a meta version per ledger, stumble on it.

entries.title: LedgerHeader ext arm 1 with flags 7 after a LEDGER_UPGRADE_FLAGS upgrade
entries.why: A flags upgrade switches the header's extension from v0 to LedgerHeaderExtensionV1 and changes no ledger entry. Readers that assume ext is always v0, or that look for upgrade effects only in entry changes, fail on this header or miss that pools were disabled.

entries.title: Ledger whose classic and Soroban transactions each bid exactly the base fee, so every charged inclusion fee is the bid
entries.why: Every transaction here bids exactly the base fee per operation, so the transaction set's discounted base fee and each bid coincide and the charged fee equals the envelope fee. It is the reference against which the synthetic entries that leave the component base fee out are read: a reader must report the same fees for both.

entries.title: LEDGER_UPGRADE_MAX_SOROBAN_TX_SET_SIZE: the upgrade rewrites the contract execution lanes setting, not a header field
entries.why: Unlike the classic transaction-set size, the Soroban limit lives in the CONFIG_SETTING_CONTRACT_EXECUTION_LANES ledger entry: the upgrade (arm 7) shows up as a STATE/UPDATED pair in upgradesProcessing and nowhere in the header. Readers that switch over LedgerUpgrade arms without it, or look for upgrade effects only in the header, fail or miss the change.

entries.title: Classic payment at Protocol 22 under default meta flags: TransactionMeta v3 with no sorobanMeta
entries.why: From Protocol 20 to 22 every transaction's meta is TransactionMeta v3, whose sorobanMeta is optional: a classic transaction leaves it absent. Lake data holds only v4, so readers tested on it alone, or that treat meta v3 as Soroban-only and dereference sorobanMeta, fail on a node's own Protocol 20 to 22 meta.

entries.title: Classic ledger at Protocols 13 and 19 under default meta flags: LedgerCloseMeta v0 with TransactionMeta v2
entries.why: The public data lake only holds TransactionMeta v4 (its objects were rewritten by a recent stellar-core), but a node or archive running an older protocol with default flags emits TransactionMeta v2 with no events. Readers tested only against lake data fail on these ledgers or report no value movement.

entries.title: Soroban ledger at Protocol 22 under default meta flags: TransactionMeta v3 with SorobanTransactionMeta
entries.why: Before Protocol 23 a Soroban transaction's meta is TransactionMeta v3: the return value and events sit in SorobanTransactionMeta, the fee refund in tx_changes_after, and with default flags there is no fee breakdown and no event at all. Readers built against v4 lake data look in the wrong places.

entries.title: First ledger of a fresh standalone chain: LedgerCloseMeta v0 upgrading protocol 0 to 30
entries.why: A chain that starts from genesis closes its first ledger under protocol 0, so its LedgerCloseMeta is v0 even though its header already says 30, and its version upgrade creates every configuration setting. Readers that pick the meta arm from the header's protocol, or that assume a v0 ledger has no Soroban settings, fail on it.

entries.title: ScVal of 100 nested vectors around a Void, one beyond what the Soroban host converts
entries.why: Valid XDR one level deeper than any value a contract can produce: the host converts at most 99 nested vectors around a Void as an argument, return value or event data and refuses 100 (cap-0046/scval-nested-vec-99-in-event carries the 99 form in meta). XDR decoders, stellar-core's print-xdr among them, must accept it; a reader whose default decode depth stops below it rejects valid XDR, and the 99 form that a successful transaction carries is only one level shallower.

entries.title: ScVal of 99 nested vectors around a Void, the deepest the Soroban host converts
entries.why: The host converts at most 99 nested vectors around a Void as an argument, return value or event data and refuses 100, so a contract can return or emit this value (cap-0046/scval-nested-vec-99-in-event carries it in meta). A reader whose default decode depth is lower rejects a value that a successful transaction can carry.

entries.title: Earliest pubnet transaction: LedgerCloseMeta v0, a TX_V0 envelope with MEMO_TEXT "hello world", three operations
entries.why: Ledger 3 holds the first transaction of the public network: the root account creates an account, pays it almost every lumen and sets its own master weight to 0, under a MEMO_TEXT "hello world" and in the pre-Protocol-13 ENVELOPE_TYPE_TX_V0 form whose source is a raw ed25519 key. The lake object is a recent stellar-core's re-emission, so this Protocol 1 ledger carries TransactionMeta v4 with backfilled transfer events whose to_muxed_id is the memo text. Readers that require V1 envelopes, that pick the meta layout from the protocol, or that turn the memo text into an address all fail on it.

entries.title: Protocol 2 upgrade ledger: no transactions and one LEDGER_UPGRADE_VERSION whose change list is empty
entries.why: The first protocol upgrade on pubnet closes a ledger with an empty transaction set and one LEDGER_UPGRADE_VERSION to 2 whose upgradesProcessing changes list is empty. Readers that expect every upgrade to change a ledger entry, or that skip ledgers with no transactions and so miss the version change, get the protocol history wrong.

entries.title: Ledger carrying two upgrades at once: protocol version 9 and base reserve 0.5 XLM
entries.why: StellarValue.upgrades can hold up to six upgrades and this ledger has two, a protocol version and a base reserve, each with its own entry in upgradesProcessing. Readers that assume at most one upgrade per ledger, or that only look for the version arm, mis-read the header or the second upgrade.

entries.title: Protocol 13 upgrade ledger: header at 13 while all 450 envelopes are the pre-13 ENVELOPE_TYPE_TX_V0 form
entries.why: Protocol 13 introduced the V1 and fee-bump envelopes (CAP-15), but on the ledger that carries the upgrade every envelope is still ENVELOPE_TYPE_TX_V0, because the transactions were applied under Protocol 12. Readers that pick the envelope type from the header version, or that no longer accept V0 envelopes on a Protocol 13 header, fail on all 450.

entries.title: AllowTrust naming the issuer itself as trustor fails at apply with ALLOW_TRUST_SELF_NOT_ALLOWED (Protocol 15)
entries.why: From Protocol 3 to 15 an AllowTrust whose trustor is the issuer itself reaches the ledger and fails while applying; from 16 it is refused as malformed. Only ledgers of those protocols hold the arm.

entries.title: ChangeTrust by the asset's own issuer fails at apply with CHANGE_TRUST_SELF_NOT_ALLOWED (Protocol 15)
entries.why: From Protocol 3 to 15 an issuer's ChangeTrust for its own asset reaches the ledger and fails while applying; from 16 it is refused as malformed. The arm is therefore found only in ledgers of those protocols, which readers replaying history meet and newer test suites never produce.

entries.title: Protocol upgrade from 13 straight to 15: pubnet skipped Protocol 14
entries.why: Pubnet went from Protocol 13 to 15 in one LEDGER_UPGRADE_VERSION; no pubnet ledger has header version 14. Readers that dispatch on every protocol in sequence, or that assume version N follows N-1, mishandle the jump and the Protocol 14 features (claimable balances, sponsorship, signed StellarValue) that first appear at 15.

entries.title: Protocol 18 upgrade ledger: header at 18 but trades still report CLAIM_ATOM_TYPE_V0 atoms
entries.why: Protocol 18 (CAP-38) added liquidity-pool claim atoms, yet on its upgrade ledger the nine trades still report CLAIM_ATOM_TYPE_V0 atoms (seller as a raw ed25519 key) and none of the newer ORDER_BOOK or LIQUIDITY_POOL arms, because the transactions ran under Protocol 17. Readers that expect the newer atoms from the header version mis-decode the results.

entries.title: First LedgerCloseMeta v1: generalized transaction set with a classic phase and an empty Soroban phase
entries.why: The ledger after the Protocol 20 upgrade switches to LedgerCloseMeta v1: the transaction set becomes a GeneralizedTransactionSet with two phases, the classic one wrapped in a component with an explicit base fee, the Soroban one empty, and the meta gains ext.v1.sorobanFeeWrite1KB and evictedKeys. Readers still reading tx_set.txs of v0 find no transactions.

entries.title: Protocol 20 upgrade ledger: LedgerCloseMeta v0 with header 20 and 14 created Soroban config settings
entries.why: The ledger that turns on Soroban is still a LedgerCloseMeta v0 (no generalized transaction set, no Soroban fields) although its header says Protocol 20, and its upgrade creates 14 CONFIG_SETTING ledger entries. Readers that pick the meta layout from the header version, or that ignore upgrade changes, misparse it or lose the network configuration.

entries.title: First LedgerCloseMeta v2: parallel Soroban phase and fee refunds after all transactions
entries.why: The first ledger after the Protocol 23 upgrade uses LedgerCloseMeta v2: the Soroban phase is v1 (execution stages of clusters), each Soroban result carries postTxApplyFeeProcessing, and refunds are after_all_txs fee events instead of after_tx. Readers on the v1 layout find no Soroban transactions or miss the refunds.

entries.title: Protocol 23 upgrade ledger: LedgerCloseMeta v1 with header 23 and nine config-setting upgrade changes
entries.why: The Protocol 23 upgrade ledger is still LedgerCloseMeta v1 with a sequential (v0) Soroban phase, although its header is 23; the parallel phase and LedgerCloseMeta v2 start one ledger later. Its upgrade updates three config settings and creates three new ones. Readers that switch to the v2 layout by header version misparse it.

entries.title: Protocol 24 upgrade ledger: fee pool grows by 31879035 stroops more than the fees charged
entries.why: The Protocol 24 upgrade adds 31879035 stroops to the header's feePool with no transaction or ledger-entry change behind it, and resets the live Soroban state size window. Readers that reconcile feePool from transaction fees, or total coins from meta, find a gap only the header explains.

entries.title: Path payment crossing 1000 offers and then a pool, valid only from Protocol 29
entries.why: Until Protocol 29 a pool hop counted against the 1000 offers one operation may cross, so a payment that crossed 1000 offers could not continue through a pool. From Protocol 29 it can, and the result holds 1001 claim atoms; readers with a 1000-atom cap, or that validate against the old limit, reject or truncate a valid result.

entries.title: Encoding a signed-payload strkey with a 65-byte payload must be refused

entries.title: Encoding a signed-payload strkey with an empty payload must be refused

entries.title: G-address written in lower case
entries.why: SEP-0023 strkeys use the upper-case RFC 4648 alphabet and are valid only if re-encoding yields the same string; accepting lower case makes two strings name one account.

entries.title: G-address with a trailing base32 padding character
entries.why: SEP-0023 forbids base32 padding; a decoder built on a padding-tolerant base32 library accepts the string, so two strings name one account.

entries.title: Hash-x strkey (X), a signer type the SEP's published vectors do not cover
entries.why: SEP-0023 publishes no X vector, yet X signers appear in account signer lists and ledger-entry changes; this one uses the SEP's 32 bytes as the hash.

entries.title: Muxed-contract strkey for the all-zero contract id with muxed id 0
entries.why: An all-zero payload is the degenerate W address; a reader that treats zero bytes as 'absent' or normalises the contract id drops or changes it.

entries.title: Muxed-account strkey with muxed id 2^53+1, the first id a float64 cannot hold
entries.why: 9007199254740993 rounds to 9007199254740992 in a float64, so a reader that converts the id to a JavaScript number or a JSON double returns a different account route without an error.

entries.title: Muxed-account strkey with muxed id 2^63-1, the largest id a signed 64-bit integer holds
entries.why: The boundary just below the SEP's 2^63 vector: a reader that stores ids as signed 64-bit integers must keep this one and fail loudly, not wrap, on the next.

entries.title: Muxed-account strkey with the largest muxed id, 2^64-1
entries.why: The muxed id is an unsigned 64-bit value; readers that hold it in a signed or floating-point type change it, and the SEP's vectors stop at 2^63.

entries.title: Pre-authorized-transaction strkey (T), a signer type the SEP's published vectors do not cover
entries.why: SEP-0023 publishes no T vector, yet T signers appear in account signer lists and ledger-entry changes; this one uses the SEP's 32 bytes as the transaction hash.

entries.title: Secret-seed strkey (S), a type the SEP's published vectors do not cover
entries.why: SEP-0023 publishes no S vector; this one uses the SEP's key bytes so every decoder is tested on the S version byte with a known payload.

entries.title: Signed-payload strkey with a 1-byte inner payload, the shortest valid P address (69 characters)
entries.why: The shortest P address is as long as an M address; a reader that sizes P columns from the SEP's 32-byte examples, or that strips the three zero padding bytes, loses or rejects it.

entries.title: Signed-payload strkey with a 64-byte inner payload, the longest valid strkey of any type (165 characters)
entries.why: XDR allows up to 64 payload bytes, so a P address can reach 165 characters, the widest address a reader meets; fixed-width text or binary columns truncate it.

entries.title: Signed-payload strkey whose inner payload is 65 bytes, one more than the XDR maximum of 64
entries.why: The XDR type is opaque payload<64>, so a 65-byte payload has no XDR form; a decoder that checks only the SEP layout (length prefix and padding) accepts it.

entries.title: Signed-payload strkey whose inner payload is empty (declared length 0)
entries.why: XDR permits a zero-length payload but stellar-core rejects such a signer (CAP-0040: SET_OPTIONS_BAD_SIGNER, txMALFORMED in extraSigners), so no ledger can hold it; a decoder that accepts it admits an address that cannot exist.

entries.title: Signed-payload strkey with a 1-byte inner payload whose three padding bytes are 0xff instead of zero
entries.why: SEP-0023 requires the padding of a signed payload to be present and zero; the SEP's own vectors test only absent padding, so a decoder can pass all 30 and still accept non-zero padding.

entries.title: The first 56 characters of a 69-character M address: checksum-valid prefix that must not decode
entries.why: A VARCHAR(56) column truncates a 69-character M address to this string. Its CRC is not checked against the full address, so a decoder that skips the per-type length check reads it as a valid M address with a 32-byte payload, dropping the muxed id.

entries.title: XDR-JSON transaction envelope with 21 signatures (declared maximum 20) must be refused
entries.why: TransactionV1Envelope.signatures is DecoratedSignature<20>; a JSON deserialiser that does not enforce the declared maximum builds a value no XDR decoder accepts and may encode bytes the network refuses.

entries.title: Custom XDR union switched on a float, with discriminant 0.1, must be refused
entries.why: RFC 4506 allows only integer, enum and bool union discriminants; an XDR runtime that lets a schema switch on a float encodes a discriminant that does not round-trip (0.1 decodes as 0.10000000149011612).

entries.title: Transaction envelope followed by one zero byte must be refused by the transaction parser
entries.why: A complete 136-byte TransactionEnvelope with one zero byte after it is not a TransactionEnvelope. 136 is 1 mod 3, so in base64 the extra byte shares the final 4-character quantum with the envelope's last byte: a parser that checks consumption by counting base64 characters instead of decoded bytes accepts the input, and two different strings then parse to the same transaction.

entries.title: Transaction envelope followed by three zero bytes must be refused by the transaction parser
entries.why: The control for the two members before it: three extra bytes after the 136-byte envelope start a new base64 quantum, so even a parser that counts base64 characters sees unread input and refuses. A reader that refuses this but accepts one or two extra bytes checks consumption in encoded characters, not decoded bytes.

entries.title: Transaction envelope followed by two zero bytes must be refused by the transaction parser
entries.why: A complete 136-byte TransactionEnvelope with two zero bytes after it is not a TransactionEnvelope. 136 is 1 mod 3, so in base64 the extra bytes share the final 4-character quantum with the envelope's last byte: a parser that checks consumption by counting base64 characters instead of decoded bytes accepts the input, and two different strings then parse to the same transaction.

entries.title: ScVal Bool encoded as 2, outside the XDR boolean range
entries.why: An XDR bool is 0 or 1 (RFC 4506 section 4.4). stellar-core's decoder reads 2 as TRUE, a decoder that tests for 1 reads it as false, and a strict one refuses it; whichever value is read re-encodes to different bytes than the input.

entries.title: ScVal vector whose length prefix is 0xFFFFFFFF with no elements after it
entries.why: The length prefix promises 4294967295 vector elements that the input does not contain. A decoder must compare the length with the remaining input before allocating; one that allocates first can be made to request a huge array by a few bytes of input.

entries.title: ScVal bytes whose length prefix is 0xFFFFFFFF with no body
entries.why: The length prefix promises 4294967295 bytes that the input does not contain. A decoder must compare the length with the remaining input before allocating; one that allocates first can be made to request 4 GiB by a few bytes of input.

entries.title: ScVal bytes whose length prefix is 0x7FFFFFFF at the end of the input
entries.why: The length prefix promises 2147483647 bytes that the input does not contain. A decoder must compare the length with the remaining input before allocating; one that allocates first can be made to request 2 GiB by a few bytes of input.

entries.title: ScVal bytes whose length prefix is 0x40000000 (1 GiB) at the end of the input
entries.why: The length prefix promises 1073741824 bytes that the input does not contain. A decoder must compare the length with the remaining input before allocating; one that allocates first can be made to request 1 GiB by a few bytes of input.

entries.title: ScVal whose union discriminant (99) names no arm in the Protocol 30 XDR definitions
entries.why: A union discriminant must select a declared arm; 99 is past SCV_EXECUTABLE_TAG (22), the last ScValType at Protocol 30. A decoder that maps unknown arms to a default or skips them reads a value that is not there.

entries.title: ScVal address whose ScAddressType (6) is one past the last arm declared at Protocol 30
entries.why: ScAddressType 5 (muxed contract) is the last arm at Protocol 30; 6 selects nothing. A decoder that accepts it, or reads its body as some other address type, produces an address that does not exist.
